title: WITHDRAW-G: Understanding Withdrawal Therapy, Delirium Risk, Addiction Characteristics and Ways of Use in GHB -Dependency
summary:
Gamma-hydroxybutyrate (GHB) or its precursor substances gamma-butyrolactone (GBL) and 1,4-butanediol (1,4-BD) are used, among other contexts, as party drugs or in the context of chemsex and may lead to the development of dependence in a subset of users. In cases of physical dependence, affected individuals must consume GHB at intervals of only a few hours due to its short half-life in order to avoid withdrawal symptoms. Physical GHB withdrawal often develops rapidly within a few hours and is associated with a significant risk of complications, particularly treatment-resistant delirium and the need for intensive care.
There is no established standard therapy for detoxification, and current treatment strategies have not been sufficiently studied. Data is also lacking regarding the clinical course of the withdrawal syndrome and the risk of complications, as well as patterns of use, comorbidities, long-term disease progression, and sociodemographic characteristics within this patient population.
The above-mentioned study aims to address the following research question: How can the GHB withdrawal syndrome be characterized in terms of symptomatology, temporal course, and complications? Which factors influence the clinical course, and what sociodemographic characteristics define this patient population?
This is a multicenter, non-randomized case series conducted at two clinical sites, comprising a retrospective observational component and a prospective interventional component.
conditions: Addiction of gamma-hydroxybutyrate or its precursors gamma-butyrolactone, 1,4-butandiole

interventions.name:
Patients admitted either electively or as an emergency due to GHB dependence and treated for withdrawal symptoms will be included. Routine treatment is provided solely based on clinical indication and is independent of study participation.

Interventions (besides routine clinical care)
Questionna

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Daily or near-daily use of GHB, GBL, or 1,4-BD
Withdrawal symptoms upon cessation
Capacity to provide informed consent and written consent to participate in the study by the participant or their legal representative
Exclusion criteria:
No relevant use of GHB, GBL, or 1,4-butanediol
Current pregnancy
Severe psychiatric disorders independent of GHB dependence that preclude participation (e.g., acute suicidality, persistent lack of capacity to consent, acute psychiatric crises)
Patients whose German language proficiency is insufficient to fully understand the written and oral study information
